drafted_from: tool:media-analysis row in tool-rows.json, do-work/meaning_index.py and test/test_meaning_index.py
start_here: Say to your AI: "Index my bakery clips red.png and blue.png and the two talk transcripts, then find which talk is about baking bread in the morning." It writes a requests file, runs the index on your computer and tells you which recording matched and where.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it reads a requests file, answers one line per request, and your AI keeps the vectors it returns under each recording's identity.
instructions: 1. Set it up once: clone the Workshop repository, brew install ffmpeg, make a virtual environment with numpy, pillow, torch, open_clip_torch, sentence-transformers and tokenizers, and fetch the two default models into the local Hugging Face cache (the script never downloads them).

2. Say which recordings to learn and what to look for; your AI writes a requests file with one JSON line per request (embed_picture for a picture or video with a file and an identity you choose, embed_speech for a transcript's chunks, then a search line) and a config file {"in_order": true} so one file both indexes and searches.

3. It runs `media-env/bin/python trillion-workshop/tools/media-analysis/do-work/meaning_index.py config.json < requests.jsonl`; read the replies: each line echoes its id with ok or an error saying what to change, and the last line is {"result": {"answered", "failed"}}.

4. Keep each embed value under its identity; next time send those back as add lines instead of embedding again, and compare hits of one search with each other, since a score is a similarity and not comparable across searches.

worked_examples.title: Two pictures and two talks, then a speech search for baking
worked_examples.ask: Which of my talks is about baking bread in the morning?
worked_examples.given: From tools/media-analysis/test/test_meaning_index.py (the real-models test): requests.jsonl holds {"id": "r", "op": "embed_picture", "identity": "red", "file": "red.png", "media_kind": "image"}, the same for blue.png, {"id": "s1", "op": "embed_speech", "identity": "talk-bread", "chunks": [{"start": 0, "end": 4, "text": "We bake sourdough bread every morning before the shop opens."}]}, {"id": "s2", "op": "embed_speech", "identity": "talk-tax", "chunks": [{"start": 0, "end": 4, "text": "The quarterly tax filing is due at the end of the month."}]} and {"id": "q", "op": "search", "query": "baking bread in the morning", "lanes": ["speech"], "limit": 2}; config.json is {"in_order": true}. red.png is a 320x240 red picture and blue.png a blue one. The command is `media-env/bin/python trillion-workshop/tools/media-analysis/do-work/meaning_index.py config.json < requests.jsonl`.
worked_examples.hands_back: First line {"id": null, "ok": true, "ready": true}. The reply to r has ok true, frames 1 and value.dims 512 (the picture's vector, to keep under the identity red); s1 and s2 give values with their chunks and vectors. The reply to q lists speech hits best first with talk-bread on top, each hit {identity, score, start, end, text}, here talk-bread at start 0, end 4 with its sourdough sentence. Last line {"result": {"answered": 5, "failed": 0}}. Sending the kept red value back as {"id": 1, "op": "add", "kind": "picture", "identity": "red", "value": ...} answers {"id": 1, "ok": true, "rows": 1} without embedding the picture again.
